methodological_rigor.justification: The retrospective compilation of 1,074 primary and 220 validation cfMeDIP-seq samples across 11 cancer types is appropriate for a resource/biomarker paper, with a uniform MEDIPIPE pipeline, explicit QC thresholds (GoGe>1.7, relH>3.0, saturation>0.9) and 100 samples excluded for QC. Confounder control is thoughtful: ComBat-seq+DESeq2 batch correction, exclusion of sex chromosomes/ENCODE blacklist, in-silico PBL depletion (2,128,687 bins), age/sex adjustment comparisons, and separate SE/PE processing after demonstrating intrinsic differences. Classifier development uses nested cross-validation with PCA fitted only on training folds to avoid leakage, and an independent cohort for external validation; a PERMANOVA permutation-based multivariate power analysis is reported. Weaknesses: age/sex missing for >240 samples precluded including them as covariates in primary analyses, data collection/analysis was explicitly not blinded or randomized ('Statistics and reproducibility' section), the 'validation' cohort includes a protocol-divergent healthy HCC set that distorts 5′ motif baselines, and the one-sided Wilcoxon test comparing common vs unique DMRs (Fig. 2e) is weak evidence for the strength claim. Statistical treatment is otherwise appropriate (two-sided tests, BH FDR, Wilcoxon/Kruskal-Wallis for non-normal data, Dunn's post hoc, |z|>2 used descriptively rather than inferentially).

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This is a retrospective pooled case-control style biomarker discovery/validation study across convenience cohorts of cancer patients and healthy controls, best mapped to Oxford LoE 3b. Clinical relevance is high: the multicancer early detection problem is clinically important, comparator benchmarks (GRAIL Galleri 54.9% sensitivity at 99.3% specificity; cfMethyl-seq 80.7% at 97.9%) are cited directly, and the single-assay methylome+fragmentome strategy offers workflow and cost advantages. Endpoints are surrogate (classifier AUC/sensitivity/specificity, DMR identification) rather than patient-level outcomes, and no prospective screening deployment is demonstrated, but the resource and classifier framework have a clear translational path including LFS risk monitoring and subtype discrimination (e.g., primary vs mCRPC with AUC 0.996).

reporting_quality.justification: REMARK applies as this is a biomarker development/validation study across retrospective cohorts. Reporting is thorough: pipeline (MEDIPIPE v1.1.0) with version numbers for all software packages, QC thresholds, inclusion/exclusion flow (100 QC-excluded, 123 multi-sampling excluded in primary; 19+106 in validation), prespecified feature engineering, and a Nature Reporting Summary referenced. Sample-level demographics, batch structure, and per-cancer counts are tabulated. Omissions include no explicit protocol registration, no REMARK checklist cross-reference, inconsistent LFS treatment between training and sensitivity scoring, and ethics approval statement that mixes primary collection with secondary dataset use without clarifying consent for reanalysis of all nine source studies. Data sharing is strong: Zenodo deposit (ref 59, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.15191455) with source data for all main and extended figures, uniformly processed data provided as a resource, and open-source MEDIPIPE pipeline cited (ref 17).

novelty_literature.justification: The principal novelty is scale and integration: the largest harmonized pancancer cfMeDIP-seq compendium (n=1,294) to date, uniformly reprocessed across 11 cancer types plus LFS. Methodological novelty is modest—individual tools (MEDIPIPE, DELFI-style ratios, Jiang 5′ motifs, Vanderstichele nucleosome footprinting, Vessies NMF) are prior art combined here. The empirically novel contribution is the demonstration that fragmentomic features extracted from methylation-enriched (cfMeDIP) fragments carry independent discriminatory signal and that their integration with methylation outperforms either alone across cancer types and subtypes, plus derivation of 14,202 common pancancer hyper-DMRs. Direct comparators (GRAIL/Galleri, cfMethyl-seq, Shen 2018, Nassiri, Burgener, Chen prostate) are acknowledged and the gap argument—absence of a harmonized pancancer cfMeDIP+fragmentome resource—is credible but incremental rather than paradigm-shifting.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is well organized with a clear introduction establishing the gap, methods grouped by analytical stage, and results that march through QC, DMR identification, fragmentomics, and classification. The abstract is self-contained and quantitatively grounded (1,074 primary + 220 validation, 14,202 pancancer DMRs, three validation cancer types absent from training). Figure legends are informative with sample sizes embedded. Minor issues: some sentences in the batch-correction methods are dense and would benefit from unpacking, LFS cohort nomenclature (previvor/survivor/positive) is defined but used in slightly different ways in training vs sensitivity reporting, acronyms like PBL and FS are introduced appropriately, and the discussion is appropriately concise without rehashing results. Overall publication-ready prose with no clarity-impeding issues.

key_strengths: Largest harmonized pancancer cfMeDIP-seq resource to date (n=1,294) with uniform MEDIPIPE processing and independent validation cohort of 220 samples including three cancer types absent from training

Rigorous confounder control: ComBat-seq+DESeq2 batch correction, in-silico PBL depletion (2.1M bins), separate SE/PE analysis after demonstrating intrinsic protocol differences, and documented age/sex sensitivity comparisons
Proper nested cross-validation with PCA fitted only on training folds, PERMANOVA-based multivariate power analysis, and benchmarking of seven ML algorithms

Integrated methylome+fragmentome in a single assay with clear performance gains over methylation alone and head-to-head benchmarking against GRAIL (54.9% at 99.3% spec) and cfMethyl-seq (80.7% at 97.9% spec)
Strong data sharing posture: Zenodo deposition with source data for every main and extended figure, open-source upstream pipeline
key_concerns: Age and/or sex missing for >240 samples precluded their inclusion as covariates in primary DMR identification; the paper argues this is acceptable but it remains a residual confounder

Validation 'healthy' controls from the HCC study used a divergent library protocol that distorted 5′ motif baselines, reducing motif-containing classifier AUCs and complicating cross-cohort generalization claims
LoE is 3b (retrospective pooled case-control style) with surrogate endpoints only; no prospective screening performance in a target population
Mechanistic claims linking DNASE1L3 motif shifts to tumor cfDNA load are correlational and acknowledged as needing functional validation
LFS cohort handling differs between training (excluded) and post-hoc sensitivity reporting (labeled as cancer), which should be stated more consistently and reported with a prespecified rule
chief_reviewer.rationale: This is a methodologically rigorous, large-scale harmonized resource paper that advances pancancer cfDNA detection by integrating methylome and fragmentome features from cfMeDIP-seq, with credible benchmarking against commercial comparators and open data; the breadth, rigor, and translational relevance support tier 1 consideration (Nature Cancer / Nature Communications-caliber oncology venues) with minor revisions to clarify LFS handling, the HCC protocol confounder, and residual age/sex adjustment.
